title: Rendering multiple problems overwrites earlier prompts
reasoning: Every problem receives the same output directory and writes part_1.md, part_2.md, and so on directly into it. Later problems overwrite earlier prompts despite the documented per-problem directory structure. Problems with different checkpoint counts also leave a mixture of prompts from different problems while the summary reports all prompts as rendered.
reproduction: Render two problems with distinct specifications into one output directory. Their shared part_N.md filenames collide, retaining only the later problem's content.
recommendation: Place each problem's rendered files in a distinct problem-named subdirectory.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The supplied tests do not exercise render_prompts or multi-problem output isolation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Render multiple problems with distinct content and unequal checkpoint counts; assert every prompt exists under its own problem directory and no content is overwritten or mixed.
minimumFixScope: Correct the per-problem output directory in render_prompts.py and cover multi-problem rendering.
